key_insight: Engineering ferroelectric domain patterns in BiFeO3 thin films strongly boosts bias-free THz emission, with stripe domains giving the largest output by enhancing photocurrent-driven screening at domain walls.
engineering_relevance: Domain configuration is a tunable design lever for compact, voltage-free THz emitters, allowing higher efficiency without the external bias fields required by photoconductive or spintronic devices.
method: Epitaxial BiFeO3 thin films were fabricated with controlled ferroelectric states: single-domain, multidomain stripe patterns, and different polarization orientations.
Time-resolved THz emission was measured while varying pump polarization and crystal orientation to separate photocurrents by symmetry.
Amplitude- and phase-resolved analysis was used to identify the dominant ultrafast emission mechanism in each domain configuration.
evidence_signal: The stripe-domain film produced a THz field about 4× stronger than single-domain films and reached roughly half the output of a metallic spintronic reference, while remaining unsaturated at the highest pump fluences.
watch_item: The optimal emission depends on precise domain engineering and film orientation, so performance may be sensitive to fabrication quality and domain stability.
paper_title: Domain-engineered ferroelectric BiFeO$_3$ thin films for efficient bias-free THz emission
